content.evidence_note: Source-linked worked proof method; not an additional independently established theorem.
failure_modes: Two fresh independent endpoint samples destroy the small-displacement difference bound.
Selecting an endpoint after observing its edge sample invalidates the conditional concentration argument.
Replacing martingale energy by the squared total step length loses the stated benefit.
An HVP-only oracle does not supply a complete-Hessian field evaluation at unit cost.
This recipe is not itself an end-to-end optimization algorithm or a universal 2/3 guarantee.
content.goal_pattern: Prove simultaneous derivative-estimation accuracy while charging predictable displacement linearly and martingale displacement quadratically.
content.key_choice: Use m=ceil(log2(T+1))+1 and p(k)=k-2^v2(k). Cache every checkpoint and estimate. Root: average fresh samples. For k>=1, use a new independent batch to set Dhat_k=(1/b_k) sum_i[A(y_k;xi_ki)-A(y_p(k);xi_ki)] and Ahat_k=Ahat_p(k)+Dhat_k. Different edges use independent batches; each difference uses the same sample at its two endpoints.
content.key_relation: Let ell=log(C(d+1)(T+1)/delta) and beta=C ell(m+1)^2/eta^2. Choose b_0=max(1,ceil(beta sigma^2)), b_k=max(1,ceil(beta min{sigma^2,L^2||y_k-y_p(k)||^2})). Lemma 1 gives simultaneous ||Ahat_k-A(y_k)||<=eta with probability >=1-delta. Lemma 2 gives expected evaluation cost <= C E[M]+C ell(m+1)^3/eta^2 (sigma^2+sigma L E[D]+L^2 E[V]), where D=sum||a_t||, V=sum||z_t||^2 and M is the actual checkpoint count. An edge costs 2b_k evaluations, the root b_0.
proof_skeleton: Condition on an edge's already determined endpoints. Its centered sample difference has norm <=2 min{sigma,L||y_k-y_p(k)||}; conditional matrix Hoeffding, using self-adjoint dilation for vectors, controls each edge error. Union bound and telescoping along a parent path control all estimates; cached errors need not be independent conditional on the entire trajectory.

For bounded stopping times s<=t, decompose x_t-x_s into summed drift and martingale increments. The truncated squared-distance term is bounded in expectation by 2 sigma L E sum_(u=s)^(t-1)||a_u||+2 L^2 E sum_(u=s)^(t-1)||z_u||^2 using stopped martingale isometry.

Edges of one binary level occupy disjoint checkpoint and chronological intervals. Sum over at most m levels; handle ceilings only at actual checkpoints. Extend a random terminal checkpoint sequence by its terminal stopping time to the deterministic index cap.

In Algorithm 1 apply separate trees to Hessians at every iterate and gradients only after the curvature test passes. Shadow stopping, descent and Appendix B are additional obligations needed for end-to-end deterministic caps.
content.required_inputs: A vector-valued or self-adjoint-matrix-valued field A(x;xi) with mean A(x), almost-sure uniform ||A(x;xi)-A(x)||<=sigma and ||A(x;xi)-A(y;xi)||<=L||x-y||. At most T+1 adaptive checkpoints. Each new edge's two endpoints are determined before its fresh independent batch is drawn; each handle can evaluate that same field at both endpoints. For charging, x_(t+1)-x_t=a_t+z_t, with a_t measurable in F_t, E[z_t|F_t]=0 and finite second moments; checkpoints are increasing bounded stopping times.
transfer_obligations: Establish a common uniform sample regularity/noise bound, the appropriate norm, and conditional centering after both endpoints are fixed.
Prove checkpoint times are bounded stopping times, rather than retrospectively selected times.
Prove the trajectory decomposition and bounds on E[D], E[V] and E[M] in the target application.
Recalibrate batch sizes and separately convert expected estimator costs into pathwise caps and a success guarantee if required.

summary: Proof recipe for uniform derivative tracking and expected sampling cost along adaptive trajectories; requires predictable endpoints and same-sample endpoint access.
title: Binary-ancestor derivative tracking with drift–martingale charging
use_when: Track a bounded-noise Lipschitz derivative field along a trajectory with predictable drift and martingale increments; fresh-only access is a misleading near-neighbor.
